diagnosis.root_cause: The router TK_AZ_Bitola_Jadranska01 has not checked in for 7.4 hours, exceeding the danger threshold. ONU connectivity, optical levels, PON service, VLAN assignment, RADIUS authentication, and the OLT are healthy, so the fault is isolated to router reachability or its management heartbeat rather than the access path.
evidence: The router heartbeat is stale at 7.4 hours, which is in the danger range above 4 hours.
The router has a previous check-in record, so this is not a never-seen device; it indicates loss of current reachability or heartbeat.
The subscriber ONU is online and responds to live SNMP probes.
RX power is approximately -20.6 dBm and TX power approximately +2.4 dBm, both within healthy EPON ranges.
Seven days of optical telemetry show stable RX, TX, distance, bias current, voltage, and temperature, ruling out fibre degradation, laser degradation, or distance change.
All tested PONs and the OLT are healthy, with normal CPU, memory, temperature, ping, and SNMP responses.
The customer VLAN is present and the expected VLAN 1062 is active, ruling out a stuck provisioning VLAN.
RADIUS records are present and consistent, and session activity is normal rather than flapping.
The customer still has an active session and recent traffic, indicating the likely impact is router management reachability rather than a confirmed customer access outage.

remediation.action: Check management-plane reachability to the router, including routing, firewall/ACL rules, monitoring-agent or heartbeat service, and router logs. Verify power and WAN/uplink status; restart the heartbeat/monitoring service or reboot the router only if safe. Confirm a fresh check-in and monitor customer sessions and traffic afterward. Do not replace the ONU or perform fibre/PON work.

ground_truth.root_cause: The BNG TK_AZ_Bitola_Jadranska01 stopped checking in 7.4 hours ago. Customers behind it lost their sessions at the same moment. The optical plant is entirely unaffected: ONUs remain registered and are returning normal signal readings.
expected_reasoning: Router heartbeat is 7.4 hours stale, past the 4 hour danger threshold
The ONU is online with RX -20.6 and TX 2.4, both normal, and the live probe confirms it
Every peer on the port is also online with normal optical readings
OLT ping, SNMP and device metrics are all healthy
So the optical layer is working and the fault is not in the fibre plant
Sessions across customers on this router ended together 7.4 hours ago
Throughput fell to zero at the same moment while the ONUs stayed registered
Healthy ONUs with dead sessions is the router signature: the optical layer carries no traffic without the BNG
The blast radius follows the router, not the OLT, so every customer it serves is affected
distractors: ONU status is online everywhere, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The OLT health check reports healthy, which is correct but irrelevant
Optical readings are perfect, which points away from where the fault is
